news.title: Argentina back Gianni Infantino and close in on being handed World Cup 2030 perk in return
news.lede: ARGENTINA have given their backing to Fifa president Gianni Infantino amid rising pressure on his position. Infantino is under massive scrutiny after his failed bid to sell off chunks of the World Cup. The Swiss chief wanted to create a subsidiary called Fifa Forward Enterprise, which would have overseen football’s biggest tournament and allowed investors to claim a stake in it. The proposals were widely condemned by a number of federations, including Uefa – who have threatened a boycott of Fifa tournaments.

news.title: Mexico and Argentina line up behind Infantino to deepen football’s civil war
news.lede: Mexico breaks ranks with Concacaf to support Fifa chief. Growing speculation country will switch to Conmebol. The Mexican football federations have broken ranks with the rest of Concacaf by issuing their public backing for beleaguered Fifa president Gianni Infantino in a move that has deepened world football’s civil war. Concacaf has called for a thorough review of Fifa’s governance in the light of the World Cup sell-off debacle, and is backing Uefa’s demands for meaningful change, although has yet to follow their European counterparts by threatening to boycott tournaments if they do not achieve their objectives.

news.title: Argentina release statement supporting Gianni Infantino as World Cup punishments decided
news.lede: The Argentina Football Association have published a statement in support of under-fire FIFA president Gianni Infantino. Infantino has been heavily criticised within the football fraternity since the end of the 2026 World Cup in North America for his plans for the tournament going forward. The Football Association of Wales were the first body to come out and publicly withdraw their own support for Infantino ahead of his bid for re-election for his fourth term as head of world football's chief organisation. Other associations, such as England, Sweden, Finland and Serbia have followed suit, with UEFA also threatening to boycott FIFA tournaments if the president did not withdraw his plans for his privately-funded FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme - something he has now done.

news.title: FIFA’s top executives were given an ultimatum to sell stake in World Cup
news.lede: The project purported to sell a 20 per cent stake in FIFA to a group of investors led by Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner. NEW YORK – The five men should have been in a celebratory mood. FIFA had just pulled off a World Cup that broke records on a number of fronts. Its spectacular culmination, the final, was a day away from the July 19 kick-off.

news.title: Gianni Infantino: Mexico defies Concacaf to join Argentina in supporting Fifa president
news.lede: Norway Football Federation Lise Klaveness has long been a critic of Infantino. Norway have called on Fifa president Gianni Infantino to resign following his aborted attempt to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors, but Mexico and Argentina have voiced their support for the 56-year-old. Norway have gone a step further than the football associations of England, Wales, Croatia and Albania, all of whom have withdrawn support for Infantino without explicitly calling for him to resign. "He [Infantino] does not have the institutional trust required to govern Fifa stably in the times we are in," Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) president Lise Klaveness said on Friday.

news.title: Players union slams FIFA 'abuse of power' as UEFA doubles down on boycott
news.lede: Mexico and Argentina's football associations are the latest to have thrown their support behind embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino despite his botched World Cup stake sale plans. On Wednesday night, Infantino was also given the "full support" of FIFA's management board in a statement despite being forced to abandon his plan to sell stakes in a company to run the World Cup to private investors. Elsewhere African football's governing body, CAF - a long-time supporter of Infantino - "unanimously reconfirmed" its support for the president and went as far as thanking him "for his contribution to African football" as well as endorsing the statement released by FIFA. Mexico and Argentina 's football associations have now also thrown their support behind Infantino.

news.title: ‘Shock horror’ – Argentina reveal stance on Gianni Infantino after World Cup controversy
news.lede: Argentina have gone against the status quo amid increasing calls for Infantino to resign after his failed plans to launch the controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). UEFA have reiterated their threat of boycotting the World Cup given that the 56-year-old acknowledged the mistakes with FFE, but is still in post. They have 'lost confidence' in his presidency, whilst the Jordanian FA president Prince Ali bin Al Hussein made an accusation of 'blackmail' over endorsement of his re-election. However, Infantino has received backing from the AFA, who released a statement to explain that he should continue as president.

news.title: Africa backs Infantino as CAF unanimously votes in FIFA president’s favour
news.lede: Jordan FA’s president, Prince Ali bin Hussein, accused FIFA of ‘blackmail’, and delayed Arab Cup prize money now paid. UEFA continues to lead criticism of FIFA President Gianni Infantino despite global body’s defiant stance. Infantino has faced leadership crisis as UEFA, AFC and Concacaf threaten drastic actions over commercial rights plan. Battle lines being drawn within FIFA as key figures break ranks with President Gianni Infantino over failed selloff.
